verdicts.strongest_argument: The finding says 'nothing in this 42-document capture connects them to Casey's July-quarter fuel line', and the capture contains a pre-print article that does exactly that - which the finding itself cites as its fourth corroborating source. docs/a86b3418d285d28ff2989a034080417c7f27f0c1.txt is optionstradingreport's 'Casey's Faces a Record-Price Fuel Quarter', captured in snapshots/20260907T152430Z.json item 13 with no tripwire tells, and it lays out the entire thesis: 'the quarter that closed July 31 covered almost the full run of this surge'; 'Fuel margin hit 46.9 cents per gallon that quarter, a company record. The question for Q1 FY2027: did they repeat it in an even more extreme fuel environment?'; a bull case conditioned on 'fuel margins held above 44 cents per gallon'; and explicitly 'Peer read-across: Murphy USA (MUSA) and Sunoco (SUN) fuel margin commentary will provide real-time calibration on sector-wide CPG dynamics heading into this print.' The peer prints are not merely reachable either - the Murphy USA Q2 transcript, the talkbusiness.net write-up with the 40.6-versus-32.0 cpg comparison and the 'even stronger' quote, and the Couche-Tard FQ4 release are all stored bodies in this capture, and cspdailynews's '6 Fuel Insights From Casey's General Stores' Recent Results' and the Globe and Mail's 'Casey's Stock Outlook Hinges on Food, Fuel and Store Growth' are two more captured items building the same frame. So the mechanism is right, the quarter window is right, and it reaches this print - but the identification of fuel cpg as the swing variable, the prior-quarter record, the peer calibration and even a numeric bar for it are the captured consensus, not a discovery. What is left is only the residual that Casey's specifically out-executed a known-favourable environment, and the 20-session -14.2% drawdown does not establish that the environment was missed: the same capture carries 'The Supply Side: Convenience stores see reduced traffic to start 2026' and the article's own counterweight that high pump prices depress the inside basket, an equally published explanation for the de-rating.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Frames the July-quarter print as a record-price fuel quarter, cites the 46.9 cpg record, sets a 44 cpg bull/bear bar, and names Murphy USA as the peer read-across for this print.
Murphy USA's 40.6 cpg total fuel contribution against 32.0 a year earlier plus the CEO's 'could be even stronger' second-half comment.
Trade-press breakdown of Casey's own fuel-margin performance, retrieved by the query 'fuel margin cents per gallon Q1 2027 expectations'.
FY2026 average fuel margin of $0.426/gal and fuel gross profit +21% are in the annual report, alongside the FY2027 inside same-store guide of 2-5%.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: quote.json (amc, so the 09-08 close of 733.49 is pre-print and admissible): 854.21 on 08-24 to 755.47 on 08-28, a -11.6% four-session slide, with volume stepping from 202k-260k to 454.5k and 442.1k against a 350,780 20d average. The de-rating happened in one week in late August, concentrated and news-shaped rather than a slow bleed, and the capture offers no item explaining it - a real hole. run_up_20d_pct -14.16%, 19.95% off the 52-week high. Median absolute reaction 5.34% on seven prints with the last at +20.29%, so a fuel-margin surprise is demonstrably capable of a large move and the run-in has cheapened the setup.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A dated sell-side fuel-margin estimate for the July quarter materially below the mid-40s cpg the peers imply, which would turn a known environment into a quantified consensus gap.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Every number in this claim is the headline and first paragraph of a captured document. docs/0488a706646c99ae39425fa2f8360512df089568.txt is The Cerbat Gem's 'Short Interest in Casey's General Stores, Inc. (NASDAQ:CASY) Decreases By 32.3%', dated 2026-09-01, captured in snapshots/20260907T152430Z.json item 15, and it reads: 'As of August 14th, there was short interest totaling 1,143,057 shares, a decline of 32.3% from the July 30th total of 1,688,551 shares... the short-interest ratio is currently 4.0 days. Currently, 3.1% of the company's shares are sold short.' The 09-08 sweep independently captured the Nasdaq short-interest settlement page for the same series. There is nothing to discover: the finding restates a captured item verbatim. Beyond publication, a 3.1% short base and 4.0 days to cover at a $26bn-plus consumer staple is the structural default, not a condition - age is not novelty. And the claim's own conclusion is negative and small by construction: it says only that a squeeze component is absent, which is a haircut on another finding's magnitude rather than an independent edge.

prior_publication.what_it_says: States the 1,143,057-share 14 August figure, the 32.3% decline from 1,688,551, the 4.0-day ratio and the 3.1% short float - the entire finding.
Casey's short interest, settlement dates and share volume series, captured the day of the print.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: quote.json: 08-27 and 08-28 volumes of 454,500 and 442,100 against the baseline's avg_volume_20d of 350,780 - 1.29x and 1.26x, consistent with the finding's own reading that this was ordinary distribution, not a cover or a panic. Nothing in the bars is attributable to short positioning.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A post-14-August borrow or utilisation reading, not in the capture, showing short interest rebuilding into the print rather than falling.

interactions: CASY#1 is explicitly a magnitude cap on CASY#0 rather than an independent claim, so it cannot add rankable edge in its own right; and both are undercut by the same document set - the 2026-09-07 sweep, the only news-bearing sweep on this day, carries the fuel-margin frame, the peer prints and the short-interest article together. CASY#0's cited 'fourth source' (optionstradingreport) is the strongest single piece of evidence against CASY#0.
corpus_limits: Two captured items carry tripwire tells (the Stocktwits 'Analyst Upgrade Ahead of Q3 Earnings' body, sha a197088939950feecbdb8135fbfe2943449c68de, and the Trefis reaction piece, sha ba3ca4ab1841d59ddad1f480247303a8c5724d41); I used neither in either direction. The businesswire timing release, the investing.com preview 'can foodservice offset traffic woes', the barchart implied-volatility story and the investing.com 'may move 6.9% on earnings' item all failed to fetch, so the capture has no usable implied move and no full sell-side preview - I therefore cannot test the claim that consensus gives no credit for record cpg against an actual dated fuel-margin estimate.
